episode_title: 96. 3 Bonus Ways to Generate Leads on LinkedIn Without Cold Outreach

real_qa.q: How can you generate leads on LinkedIn using polls in groups without cold outreach?
real_qa.r: In LinkedIn groups, you can post a poll question once per week asking about business-specific problems. When members vote, you can click on the vote count to see every person who voted and their profile headline. You then identify those who fit your ideal client or business ally persona, right-click to open their profile, and send a personalized connection request referencing the poll. This creates warm connections rather than cold outreach.

real_qa.q: What is the benefit of using LinkedIn newsletter subscribers for lead generation?
real_qa.r: LinkedIn newsletter subscribers are a separate subset from your first-degree connections and followers, allowing you to reach people not yet connected to you. You can view all your newsletter subscribers, filter them by their headline to identify ideal clients or business allies, and send personalized connection requests thanking them for subscribing. This turns your subscriber list into a warm outreach channel.

real_qa.q: How do you message first-degree connections who vote on your LinkedIn polls?
real_qa.r: When conducting polls on your personal LinkedIn profile, first-degree connections are more likely to vote than in group polls. You can identify these connections by a blue arrow icon next to their name, then click to open LinkedIn DMs with the poll post included. You message them thanking them for voting and offering to help or collaborate, making this the warmest lead generation approach since they are already connected.

real_qa.q: What are the criteria for identifying people to reach out to after LinkedIn polls or newsletter engagement?
real_qa.r: When reviewing people who voted or engaged, Scott Aaron filters them into two categories: ideal clients (people you can serve with coaching, consulting, courses, programs, masterminds, or communities) and business allies (people for introductions, collaborations, or referral partnerships). Only those fitting these two personas are contacted for connection requests or outreach.
